[Thu Oct 8 #acct-northwind-eng] rachel: Noted, Tomas. Darnell, let me know when you've had a look so I can build the renewal deck around it.

[Thu Oct 8 #acct-northwind-eng] gabe: On missing fields: yes. Have the model return a list of empty required fields in structured output, and the UI can highlight them for staff.

[Tue Oct 6 #acct-northwind] rachel: Good angle. Keiko, can you get a customer quote on the summarization wins in their own words? Would help anchor the expansion pitch.
[Tue Oct 6 #acct-northwind] keiko: On it. One of the pilot nurse managers gave a great line on the summarization wins last week, so I'll ask if we can use it.
[Tue Oct 6 #acct-northwind] gabe: Fair warning, the QBR deck is already at like 40 slides. Pretty sure the nurse manager's quote is getting its own slide at this point.
[Tue Oct 6 #acct-northwind] rachel: Gabe, cut it to a handful of slides. Execs skim. Keep the nurse manager quote and the usage trend, drop the rest to appendix.
[Tue Oct 6 #acct-northwind] gabe: Will do. I'll keep the usage trend to one clean chart and move the per-team breakdown to the appendix.

[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] nadia: Ok, we need to nail down the release gate and what goes in the held-out set today. Marcus, where are we on licensing for the scraped repos?
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] marcus: Mostly sorted. Most repos are MIT or Apache, but a handful have no license file at all, so I'm leaning toward dropping those until we hear back from maintainers.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] yuki: Dropping the unlicensed ones makes sense to me. Do we know if they skew toward any particular task type? Don't want the held-out set lopsided afterward.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] marcus: Checking now. Gut feeling is the unlicensed ones cluster in small CLI tools and research code, so refactoring and bug-fix tasks might take the hit.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] yuki: Ok, that matters for the gate then. Release gate threshold is 70% pass@1, so if the bug-fix slice shrinks a lot we should check the variance on it.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] theo: I can rerun the bug-fix slice with a few seeds on the current baseline to see how noisy it is once those repos are out.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] yuki: also, that number is measured on the held-out set only, not dev. Dev scores shouldn't count toward it.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] marcus: Bug-fix looks like the worst hit. A lot of the unlicensed ones are single-file scripts with small, self-contained failing tests, which are the cleanest bug-fix items.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] marcus: Decision for the held-out set: it's 1,200 items, locked in after the unlicensed repos come out. If bug-fix ends up too thin, I'll backfill from licensed repos rather than shrink the total.
---
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] theo: Once the swap list is final I'll rerun the baselines and plot pass rate by repo size. Curious if multi-file tasks widen the gap between models.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] yuki: Theo, if you plot by repo size, bucket by files touched too. Otherwise size and multi-file get tangled and the gap is hard to read.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] theo: Good call, will do. I'll also split by language since the Python tasks tend to be the easiest, so that might be another confound.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] marcus: Found a couple of multi-file candidates in a Rust build tool, bug spans the parser and the config loader. Checking the license now.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] yuki: Rust is useful there too. If the models do much worse on those, I'd want to report language as its own breakdown in the paper.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] theo: Rust tasks would be a good breakdown. Since the paper's due Oct 30, I'll plan to have the baseline reruns done a few days before so we have time to write up the language split.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] marcus: Rust build tool license came back permissive, so those candidates are usable. The fix touches the parser and config loader together, and the tests are deterministic.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] elena: Rust builds will be slow in the sandbox. I'll check the image has the toolchain cached so timeouts don't masquerade as model failures.
---
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] felix: I'll add a language field and a files-touched field to the task metadata, so Theo's breakdowns come straight from the release without a separate script.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] yuki: Felix, can the language field hold more than one value? The Rust parser fix also touches TOML config, and I'd rather not force a single label.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] felix: Yes, I'll make language a list instead of a single label. Then the Rust parser fix can carry both Rust and TOML, and Theo can group on either.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] yuki: With language as a list, I'll report breakdowns by primary language only, so multi-label tasks don't get double counted in the paper tables.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] theo: Primary-language only works for me. I'll flag in the table caption which tasks are multi-label so reviewers don't wonder why TOML never shows up.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] elena: Fair warning, the eval jobs have more retries than I do at the gym. Rust timeouts are gonna be the worst offenders.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] marcus: I'll also check whether the Rust build tool's test suite pulls anything from the network. If it does, the sandbox will fail those no matter what the model writes.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] yuki: If it does pull from the network, vendoring the dependencies into the image would fix that. Otherwise we'd have to drop those tasks and look for others.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] elena: Vendoring works for me. I can bake the crates into the sandbox image so builds run offline. Marcus, send me the lockfile once you pick the tasks.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] marcus: Will do. Checking now whether the lockfile is pinned for that Rust tool. If it isn't, I'll resolve versions first so the crates don't drift.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] yuki: If the lockfile isn't pinned, note which crate versions you resolve to. I'd like the paper's appendix to list the toolchain so the Rust tasks are reproducible.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] marcus: Lockfile's checked in but a couple of entries use loose version ranges. I'll resolve them and write down what each crate lands on.
